storyTitle: TSMC approves up to $1 billion split between Anthropic and OpenAI
insight: TSMC is buying stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI, the two labs most dependent on its chips: the supplier is becoming a shareholder.
linkedin:
TSMC now owns a piece of the labs it supplies.

Its board approved up to $1 billion: $500 million into Anthropic shares tied to its IPO price, $500 million into OpenAI preferred stock.

The chipmaker is no longer just selling to the two labs most dependent on its chips.

That ties chip supply and AI model economics closer together.

page:
Today's edition: TSMC's board approved up to $1 billion in direct stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI, so the world's dominant chipmaker now holds equity in the two labs most dependent on its chips.

AI & Tech: Meta and OpenAI both moved to buy AI coding-agent startups on the same day, and New York's RAISE Act opened its AI registration portal.

Business: Palo Alto Networks is paying $4.5 billion for Applied Compute, and Tata Sons' long-delayed board meeting finally took up Noel Tata's restructuring plan.

Markets: The Sensex and Nifty fell about 1% as Brent crude passed $97, while the S&P 500 posted its best week in 19 months.

thread: Black Friday online spending in the US passed $9.7B by Friday evening, a new record. Meanwhile chips, AI and oil all moved. Here's what mattered 👇
TSMC's board approved up to $1B in stakes: $500M in Anthropic, $500M in OpenAI. The chipmaker now owns a piece of the two labs that depend on its chips most.
Meta bought Conductor, an app for running many AI coding agents at once. The same day OpenAI said it will buy Pierre Computer Company. Owning the AI coding stack is now a real platform fight.
Palo Alto Networks is paying $4.5B in stock for Applied Compute, a startup of about 50 people with a $100M run-rate. A security firm buying AI infrastructure says securing AI is not optional.
Sensex fell 1.17% and Nifty fell 1.07% as Brent crude crossed $97 on West Asia attacks. Oil, not company results, ended India's two-day recovery.
Wall Street went the other way. The S&P 500 rose 1.6% in a short session and gained 5.6% for the week, its best in 19 months. AI and chip stocks led the rebound.

Oil hit India while AI money lifted the US. Monday's GDP print is the next test.

leaders.title: Misenchanted, Not Disenchanted: Is the Meaning Crisis a Story We Tell Ourselves?
leaders.post:
Telling people life is hollow can make it feel hollow.

Humanist chaplain James Croft calls the "meaning crisis" story an illness caused by its own cure.

The symptoms are real: loneliness, anxiety, housing costs, job fear. But he says our world isn't disenchanted, it's misenchanted by bad stories and bad habits of attention.

He also notes we only hear from the literate few of the past, so a golden age is easy to imagine.
